# Remove stray tracked `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts.orig` artefact

## Problem statement

A 789-line editor/merge backup, `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts.orig`, was committed (4b407b66, during AH-0MVD2N333004VDA9) and is still tracked in git. It ships with the repo and is picked up by any tool that globs the source tree (build/test/typecheck scans, grep, editor symbol search), where it presents as a second, stale copy of the wormhole-spawn module. `.gitignore` has no `*.orig` rule, so the next editor or merge backup can be committed again.

## Users

- **Maintainer** reading the VFX tree or `src/vfx/` diffs — currently sees an unexplained 789-line backup beside the real 1465-line module.
- **Agent/developer** searching for `wormholeSpawn` — gets a misleading duplicate that is out of date relative to the shipped module.

User story: *As a maintainer, the repository contains only intentional source files, so the VFX source tree is not cluttered by a stale backup copy of `wormholeSpawn.ts`.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts.orig` is removed from the working tree and from git tracking (`git rm src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts.orig`), appearing as a staged deletion in the branch diff.
- `git ls-files '*.orig'` returns no paths in the main checkout, i.e. no other tracked editor/merge backup remains.
- No code, test, config or docs reference `wormholeSpawn.ts.orig` (searches for the literal name and for `*.orig` globs come back clean).
- `.gitignore` gains a commented `*.orig` rule (or equivalent) so future merge/editor backups cannot be committed; the comment names this work item so the rule's purpose is discoverable.
- `npm run build` and the unit suite pass, and `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` plus `wormholeSpawn.test.ts` behaviour is unchanged — the change removes a file only, it does not alter shipped VFX behaviour (gym↔game parity is untouched).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (expected: `.gitignore` comment only).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The VFX source tree contains only real source files again, so maintainers and tooling stop tripping over a stale 789-line duplicate of `wormholeSpawn.ts`, and a `.gitignore` rule stops the same backup from being committed in future.

## Constraints

- Do not modify `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` or its test — the deletion must be behaviour-neutral.
- `.gitignore` changes stay in the existing "End of Worklog Specific Ignores" block, matching the file's current comment style.
- Other worktrees under `.worklog/worktrees/` also contain a copy of the file; they are out of scope and must not be touched from this checkout.
- CHANGELOG.md is managed by the release pipeline — do not edit it.

## Existing state

- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts.orig` — 789 lines, tracked at `HEAD`, added in 4b407b66; a pre-shimmer snapshot (current module is 1465 lines) with no conflict markers.
- `.gitignore` — no `*.orig` (or equivalent backup) rule today.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` (1465 lines) and `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.test.ts` — the live module and its contract; unaffected by this change.
- Repo-wide check: `git ls-files | grep -i '\.orig$'` returns exactly this one path.

## Desired change

Delete the tracked backup and add a repository-wide ignore rule for `*.orig` backup files.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: the old snapshot is lost.** Accepted — the backup remains recoverable from git history (4b407b66); it is a stale copy, not unique work.
- **Risk: the ignore rule masks a future intentional `.orig` file.** Low — no tracked `.orig` file other than this one exists, and `.orig` is conventionally an editor/merge backup extension.
- **Assumption:** no build, test, lint or typecheck glob relies on the file's presence (it is not imported anywhere).
- **Scope-creep guard:** other hygiene findings (other stray artefacts, worktree copies, dependency-cache debris) are recorded as linked work items rather than folded into this one.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts.orig` — Delete: untrack and remove the stale backup.
- `.gitignore` — Edit: add `*.orig` with a comment naming this work item.

## Related work

- AH-0MVD2N333004VDA9 — "Per-enemy emergence shimmer" (completed): the feature whose commit 4b407b66 accidentally carried the backup file.
- AH-0MVNTXXTA0081S38 — the item during which this stray artefact was found (source of `discovered-from`).
- AH-0MV8IHVT1008M2LG, AH-0MU480XW8009160C — precedent `.gitignore` hygiene items (completed), same pattern of adding a narrowly-scoped ignore rule.
- AH-0MVSDZMGJ005QO0Z — "Remove leftover src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts.orig conflict artifact" (open, created 38 min after this item): overlapping duplicate. Its ACs repeat the deletion/`git ls-files '*.orig'`/suite checks but omit the `.gitignore` rule, so this item is the superset and stays the implementation target; the duplicate check below records the resolution.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were needed: the seed description already carried a goal, user story and four testable acceptance criteria. The following was verified directly against the repository rather than asked of the operator:

- Q: Does the artefact still exist and is it still tracked at `HEAD`? — Answer (repo evidence): yes. `git ls-files | grep -i '\.orig$'` → `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts.orig`; the file is present on disk (789 lines).
- Q: Is the file referenced anywhere? — Answer (repo evidence): no. No code/test/config/doc matches for `wormholeSpawn.ts.orig`; module imports point at `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn` only.
- Q: Is an ignore rule already present? — Answer (repo evidence): no. `.gitignore` contains no `*.orig`-style rule.
- Q: Is there duplicate work in the worklog? — Answer (repo evidence, revised after `find-related`): **partial duplicate found.**
  `wl search "orig backup stray artefact"` returns only this item, but the automated related-work report surfaced
  AH-0MVSDZMGJ005QO0Z ("Remove leftover src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts.orig conflict artifact", open, created 2026-10-28T17:26Z,
  38 minutes *after* this item). Its acceptance criteria cover the same deletion and `git ls-files '*.orig'` check
  but omit the `.gitignore` `*.orig` rule, so this item's AC set is a superset. Resolution: this (earlier) item stays the
  implementation target and the overlap is recorded on both items; closing the duplicate is left to the producer rather
  than unilaterally closing another open work item.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVSDZMGJ005QO0Z** – Remove leftover src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts.orig conflict artifact (open)
- **AH-0MVSEBCNC005G7XW** – Hyperspace warp transition VFX (completed)
- **AH-0MT9XNDZB003IAO1** – Remove accidentally-committed node_modules symlink from repo (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, accepted, add, added, adding (+213 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: acceptance, add, added, adding, again (+212 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: acceptance, add, added, adding, again (+186 more)

## Clarification from duplicate intake (AH-0MVSDZMGJ005QO0Z)

AH-0MVSDZMGJ005QO0Z raised the same deletion independently (discovered-from:AH-0MVNTXZ4X00031AU)
and was closed as a duplicate of this item; its verification wording is folded in here:

- Verified at intake time: `git ls-files '*.orig'` lists **only** `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts.orig` — no other conflict/editor artefacts are tracked, so this one deletion is the complete sweep.
- Verified at intake time: nothing imports or path-loads the file (`rg 'wormholeSpawn'` matches only the live module and its consumers); the `.orig` extension also keeps it out of the TypeScript build graph, so the change is inert.
- Added verification step: after the deletion, `git ls-files '*.orig'` must return nothing (proves the removal from tracking, not just from the working tree).
- Rationale for the `.gitignore` rule (AC4): the current `.gitignore` has no `*.orig`/`*.rej` entry, which is how this artefact could be committed in the first place.

# Intake Brief: Derive the ring-timing docs guard's measured means from the committed baseline artifact

**Problem:** The guard in `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` pins four measured ring-timing means as literals, but the GDD §8.2 values are a transcription of `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`. When the artifact is recalibrated (as happened twice), the guard goes red and requires manual edits — the wrong source of truth.

**Users:** Developers maintaining ring-timing consistency between the artifact, GDD §8.2, and the test guard.

**User stories:**
*As a maintainer,* I want the docs guard to derive its expected values from the committed baseline artifact, so that recalibrating the artifact automatically updates the guard without manual edits.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The guard's four measured-mean assertions are derived from `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`; no measured-mean literal remains in the test.
2. Editing a mean in the artifact alone (without the GDD) fails the guard; editing the GDD to a value the artifact does not hold fails the guard.
3. The window and tolerance assertions are unchanged and still pass.
4. Full project test suite passes.

**Impact:** The docs guard becomes self-consistent — recalibrating the artifact no longer strands the guard, and the GDD can never silently drift from measured values.

**Constraints:**
- Use `summary.totalMinutes.mean.toFixed(1)` per `ringIndex`/`strategy` pair (`1-grind`, `2-grind`, `1-rush`, `2-rush`).
- Window (40–60, 90–120) and tolerance (±2 / ±3 min) assertions must remain explicit — they are design values owned by `RING_TIMING_TARGETS` / `RING_TIMING_TOLERANCE_PERCENT`, not measurements.
- The implementation must work at test-runtime (Node.js, no TypeScript compilation dependency).

**Existing state:** `outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` uses hardcoded regex literals (`54.3`, `116.4`, `32.0`, `62.7`).

**Desired change:** Read the baseline artifact at test runtime, compute expected one-decimal means from `summary.totalMinutes.mean.toFixed(1)`, and assert GDD §8.2 prose quotes match those values.

**Producer decision (plan 2026-11-13):** The committed artifact holds ring2-rush mean `62.64546296296296` → `toFixed(1)` = **62.6**, but the GDD §8.2, `docs/EVALUATION.md` and `README.md` (and the current guard literal) all quote **62.7** — the transcription drift the guard exists to catch. Producer approved correcting the **62.7 → 62.6** quotes in GDD §8.2 (table and prose) and, for consistency, `docs/EVALUATION.md` and `README.md`, as part of this item (see Appendix Q1). The corrected docs must hold the derived value so the guard passes; this is a required consequence of AC2, not scope creep.

**Key Files (predicted):**
- `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` — modify the guard test to derive values from artifact
- `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` — source of truth (read-only)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — correct the ring2-rush measured-mean quote (62.7 → 62.6) in §8.2 table and prose
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` — correct the ring2-rush measured-mean quote (62.7 → 62.6)
- `README.md` — correct the rush-line quote (62.7 → 62.6)

**Risks & assumptions:**
- *Scope creep:* Guard change must NOT touch window/tolerance logic or artifact regeneration — those are separate concerns.
- *Assumption:* The artifact structure (`ringIndex` + `strategy` → `summary.totalMinutes.mean`) is stable and will remain so.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWB8VETE006YMVI** – Regenerate the ring-timing baseline evidence (completed)
- **AH-0MWCQ4GTE005YG02** – Regenerate the ring-timing baseline artifact (blocked)
- **AH-0MWB8VFBC003743Y** – Requote docs and reconcile ring-timing guards (completed)
- AH-0MW0J01VV0054BRR — sibling item that landed literal-pinning form first; parked implementation at commit `9467a48a`
- AH-0MW09QIJU000DAGT — recalibrated ring-2 window and regenerated artifact (commits `a7c57da1`, `032d96e9`)

### Repository file matches

## Appendix

- Q1: "The committed artifact holds ring2-rush mean `62.64546296296296` → `toFixed(1)` = 62.6, but the GDD §8.2, EVALUATION.md, README and the current guard all quote 62.7. Under the item's mandated derivation the new guard computes 62.6 and goes red against the current GDD until the docs are corrected. Recommended: correct the GDD §8.2 quote (and EVALUATION.md + README for consistency) from 62.7 to 62.6 as part of this item. Alternative: scope the doc correction separately and land red (contradicts AC4)." Answer (producer): **"Proceed as recommended"** — correct the 62.7 → 62.6 quotes in GDD §8.2, EVALUATION.md and README as part of this item; the derived guard enforces 62.6. Final: docs correction in scope.

No children created — single-slice chore; implement directly.

## Goal

Make the dev-only telemetry recorder cheap enough that it does not distort a measured run.

**User story:** As a developer profiling the game, I want the dev telemetry recorder to stay out of the frame budget, so a profile measures the game and not the recorder.

## Evidence (measured, AH-0MVXV0E8000937U5)

CPU profile of \`PlayScene\` level 10 demo (60 s, desktop headless Chromium), with the dev recorder enabled:

- \`sanitiseObject\` (\`src/telemetry/redact.ts:93\`) 0.18 % of the measured window, \`sanitise\` (\`src/telemetry/redact.ts:65\`) 0.15 %, \`utf8ByteLength\` (\`src/telemetry/devUpload.ts:180\`) 0.14 %, \`write\` (\`src/telemetry/sinks.ts:50\`) 0.08 %, \`deepFreeze\` (\`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:459\`) 0.16 % — **~0.7 % of the window / ~7 % of JS**.
- The same run logged a skipped run-end upload: 15.8 MiB of run telemetry exceeded the 8 MiB browser→node message cap, so the recorder was serialising a payload it then discarded.

## Scope

- Avoid serialising/redacting a payload that will be discarded for exceeding the upload cap (check the size first, or stream/bound the recording).
- Keep redaction guarantees intact: no unredacted payload may ever reach a sink.

## Out of scope

- Production telemetry behaviour (the recorder is dev-only).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A run whose telemetry exceeds the upload cap no longer pays the full serialise+redact cost before discarding (verified by a test on the size-guard seam).
2. Redaction tests still pass (no path skips redaction for a payload that is written).
3. In the same profiled demo run, the telemetry bucket share is measurably lower, with the before/after numbers recorded on this item.
4. Full project test suite passes.

## Problem statement

The ring-timing CLI's operator-facing text report mixes per-seed and multi-seed
figures. `formatRingTimingReport` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) renders:

- means over the seed set for `deployments`, `measured runs`, `total`, `banked salvage` and `ring secured`;
- but **seed 1's own value** for `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` (`report.runs[0]?.retryMinutes`, `runs[0]?.betweenSortieMinutes`, `runs[0]?.retakeMinutes` / `runs[0]?.expectedRetakes`).

With the default three-seed evidence set the two halves of one report therefore
describe different populations.

## Evidence

`npm run ring-timing` (2026-11-11, worktree of AH-0MW9VATHR0003WTJ, exit 0):

```text
Ring 2 · grind · seeds 1, 2, 3
  retries            55.0 min
  total              116.4 min (min 112.7, max 123.4)
```

The committed artefact (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, revision
`e873e8c3`) records per-seed `retryMinutes` of **55 / 50 / 55** — a mean of
**53.3**, not 55.0. `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline* consequently
quotes "55 of its 116.4 min (≈47 %)", pairing seed 1's retry total with the
mean total (the mean-based share is ≈45.8 %). `between sorties` and
`exposed re-capture` happen to be seed-invariant today, so only the retry line
is visibly wrong — but the rendering is one bug, not one line.

## Expected behaviour

Every metric line in the text report describes the same population (the seed
set), consistent with the JSON artefact: mean plus min–max for the per-run
totals, or an explicitly labelled seed-1 sample. The report-rendering test
(`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` § *report rendering*) should pin a
multi-seed case where the seeds differ, so the mixing cannot return.

## Acceptance criteria

- `formatRingTimingReport` renders `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` from the multi-seed aggregate (mean, with min–max where the JSON summary carries it), or labels them as a single seed; no line silently reports seed 1 as the seed-set figure.
- A report-rendering test feeds a multi-seed report whose per-seed retry totals differ and asserts the rendered value is the mean, not seed 1's.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline* quotes the retry minutes and share from the aggregate consistent with the rendered report and the committed artefact.
- Full project test suite passes.

## Notes

- Found by the verification slice `Record the ring 2 before/after split and verify the acceptance criteria (AH-0MW9VATHR0003WTJ)`; deliberately not fixed there (that item's scope forbids code changes).
- No behaviour or measured value changes: this is a reporting/consistency fix only.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5** – Rebalance ring 2's grind budget: measured 48.1 min vs the authored 90–120 min window (open)
- **AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X** – Rebalance ring 1's grind budget: measured 16.4 min vs the authored 40–60 min window (open)
- **AH-0MW9VARCU000XZIL** – Restore ring 2's 70–100 window and regenerate the ring-timing evidence (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: acceptance, aggregate, asserts, banked, based (+119 more)
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, aggregate, asserts, banked, based (+109 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: acceptance, aggregate, artefact, asserts, based (+104 more)
## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-14)

Four children, test-first dependency order (3 planned + 1 auto-closed coverage gap):

1. **Test: report rendering pins multi-seed retry aggregates (AH-0MWGVXB95002W7KI)** — task, low. Pins parent AC 2: a multi-seed report whose per-seed retry totals differ must render the aggregate mean, never seed 1's; also pins the between-sorties and exposed-re-capture lines.
2. **Implement: render retry/between-sortie/recapture from the seed aggregate (AH-0MWGVXJ5V008QV50)** — bug, low. Adds `betweenSortieMinutes` / `retryMinutes` / `retakeMinutes` / `expectedRetakes` `RingTimingStats` to `RingTimingSummary`, renders the three report lines from the aggregates in `formatRingTimingReport`, and regenerates the committed baseline artefact (deterministic; additive summary fields). Depends on 1.
3. **Docs: EVALUATION.md retry share from the aggregate (AH-0MWGVXRFS009HBR5)** — docs, low. Quotes the retry minutes + share from the aggregate in `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline*, consistent with the rendered report and the committed artefact. Depends on 2.
4. **Close coverage gap: Full project test suite passes. (AH-0MWGW08C0006CDUX)** — task, medium, auto-created by the AC coverage review; verifies the full suite via the test skill at the dev-push gate.

Vertical slicing: each phase is a thin end-to-end slice (test → code + evidence → docs); the scope is Small, so no further phasing is needed.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-14: initial decomposition — 3 children created (test-first), dependency edges wired (implement → test; docs → implement); AC coverage review auto-closed the suite-gate gap (created AH-0MWGW08C0006CDUX) and advanced the parent to `plan_complete`; parent estimate refreshed via the effort-and-risk skill (Small / Medium, see its comment).

No operator questions were asked in this session — a downtime-dispatched run (herdr-downtime) with no interactive approver. The plan proceeds on the documented assumptions below; all are recorded for audit.

- A1 (fix shape): extend `RingTimingSummary` with the four aggregate stats and render from them — parent AC 1's primary option ("mean, with min–max where the JSON summary carries it") — rather than re-labelling the lines as a single seed. Rationale: every other report line is already aggregate and the JSON artefact is the stated consistency reference. Final: aggregate extension.
- A2 (artefact): regenerate `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` so its JSON summary carries the new fields. Deterministic per the existing determinism test; existing mean/min/max totals must be unchanged. Final: regenerate.
- A3 (doc quote): quote the grind line's aggregate retry minutes + share in § *Measured baseline* (mirrors the old "55 of its 116.4 min" quote; the rush line's re-capture is already covered by its own reading bullet). Final: grind-line aggregate quote.
- No OPEN QUESTION entries: no producer ruling is required to proceed with this plan.

# Re-measure ring timing for one-level hex deployments (AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A)

Discovered-from: AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2 (In HexMap killing the mini-boss wins the hex).

## Problem statement

The measured ring baseline (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, GDD §8.2
"Measured ring timings") models a deployment as the **classic campaign slice**
from the hex's aggression-selected level through to the campaign's final boss.
The mini-boss ending turns a deployment into exactly **one** campaign level,
ending on that level's **five-wave sortie** (its first four regular waves then its
mini-boss on wave 5 — `truncateCampaignForDeployment`, AH-0MWDCBVQ700579WS), so the per-deployment duration, the
per-ring deployment count and every derived ring window move — and the
committed evidence no longer measures the game a player plays.

## Users

- **As a Hangar War player**, I want the ring budgets to describe sorties I
  actually fly — one hex, one level, one mini-boss — so the advertised
  "40–60 minute ring" is the time I will really spend.
- **As a producer**, I want the timing evidence regenerated from the shipped
  one-level deployment, so a pacing ruling rests on measured numbers rather
  than on a model of a campaign slice that no longer exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `createArenaDeploymentRunner` plays the **shipped one-level deployment**
  (the hex's aggression-selected level, through the arena's per-level mode)
  and derives each deployment's duration from the arena's `level_cleared`
  transition: a cleared level is a **captured** deployment, a player death
  before it is a **loss**. `npm run ring-timing -- --json --out
  docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` regenerates the artifact on the shipped
  code with no hand-edited numbers.
- The retry allowance charges the **replayed deployment's own measured
  length** instead of the fixed 5-minute window, and the between-sortie
  allowance stays at the documented **2 minutes**; both are stated in the
  harness documentation and pinned by a test. A rush-line re-capture is charged
  the line's **measured mean deployment + the same 2-minute visit**, replacing
  the retired 18 000-tick window (producer ruling Q4 = a).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 (the measured table, the supported
  playstyles numbers and the "a deployment is" sentence) and the docs guards
  (`src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`, `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`)
  match the regenerated artifact. Any ring whose budget no longer holds is
  recorded with its new measurement **and opened as a separate linked
  rebalancing work item** rather than silently re-worded.
- Tests cover the new model: a per-level deployment ends at its level's
  wave-5 sortie clear, an early death is a loss, the report is deterministic for the
  same seeds/options, and the ring-1/ring-2 budget verdicts match the
  regenerated numbers.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries; the full
  project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Impact

A player's ring time is measured from the sortie they actually fly — one hex
level ending on its mini-boss — so the design doc's ring budgets describe real
play instead of the rest of the campaign.

## Constraints

- **Blocked by the mini-boss ending** (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2): tracked as a
  dependency edge. None of the epic's children are implemented and there are
  no mini-boss commits on `dev` at intake time, so a baseline regenerated
  before that behaviour ships would be re-run immediately.
- **The arena does not simulate a boss or mini-boss entity** (documented
  fidelity boundary in `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`): a mini-boss wave is its
  authored group composition. The measured sortie therefore ends when the
  wave-5 sortie composition clears; the boss encounter's own duration is **not
  modelled**. Record that gap; modelling a mini-boss encounter is a linked
  follow-up, not scope here.
- **Per-level mode does not end on `level_cleared`**: `runArena` keeps ticking
  to `config.ticks` after the level clears, and `won` in non-campaign modes is
  `lives > 0 && aliveHostiles === 0` (a lingering asteroid keeps it false). The
  duration must therefore come from the `level_cleared` event, never from
  `ticksSimulated` or `won`.
- **Only the deployment model changes.** The aggression → level mapping
  (`hexDifficultyProfile`), the authored ring/hex data, the loadout resolution
  (`resolveDeploymentLoadout`, `ringEntryOwnership`), the retake chance
  (`DEFAULT_RETAKE_CHANCE_PERCENT`) and the 2-minute between-sortie allowance
  all stay as shipped, so the before/after delta is attributable.
- **Determinism is preserved**: the same seeds and options produce an identical
  report; the harness never reads the wall clock.
- **Numbers are never hand-edited** in `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` or
  the GDD table — the artifact is regenerated and the docs requote it.
- **Scope-creep clause.** Reporting per-deployment sortie length and sortie
  counts in the GDD table, modelling the mini-boss fight itself, re-authoring
  the 40–60 / 90–120 windows, and making the docs guard derive its means from
  the artifact (AH-0MW0KSCU20096B02) are **linked items**, not scope here. A
  ring whose budget no longer holds becomes its own linked rebalancing item.

## Existing state (researched, with evidence)

- **Deployment model as committed.** `createArenaDeploymentRunner`
  (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` ≈ line 767) runs `runArena` with `campaign:
  true` and `campaignLevels: campaignFromLevel(campaign, request.level)` — the
  campaign slice from the hex's level to the final boss. Duration is
  `result.ticksSimulated × request.dt`, capped by `RING_DEPLOYMENT_TICKS`
  (= `DEFAULT_BATCH_TICKS` = 18 000 ticks ≈ 300 s); `captured` is
  `result.won || ticksSimulated >= request.ticks`, i.e. "survived the window".
- **Retry model.** `DEFAULT_RETRY_MINUTES = RING_DEPLOYMENT_TICKS × dt / 60` =
  a flat **5 minutes** per loss, independent of what the run measured.
- **Committed baseline** (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, four
  ring/line reports, seeds 1–3, competent bot):

  | Ring | Line | Total mean (min–max) | Losses | Modelled deployment minutes | Budget |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 (6 hexes) | grind | 54.3 (51.0–56.6) | 4.7 | 19.0 | 40–60 · in-window |
  | 1 (6 hexes) | rush | 32.0 (31.9–32.2) | 1.0 | 0.5 | not-applicable |
  | 2 (12 hexes) | grind | 116.4 (112.7–123.4) | 10.7 | 39.1 | 90–120 · in-window |
  | 2 (12 hexes) | rush | 62.7 (60.9–63.6) | 0.7 | 3.4 | not-applicable |

  Roughly **3.2 minutes per deployment** on both grind lines, i.e. most of a
  deployment's time is the slice climbing campaign levels rather than the
  hex's own level — the quantity the one-level deployment removes.
- **Existing per-level seam.** `runArena` already supports an explicit `level`
  (per-level mode, AH-0MVLJFB1I0099X4Z) via `buildLevelWavePlan`, emitting
  `wave_cleared` / `level_cleared`; it is the closest shipped model of a
  one-level deployment.
- **Docs guards.** `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` pins the four means
  (`54.3`, `116.4`, `32.0`, `62.7`), the windows (40–60, 90–120), the tolerance
  (±2 min, ±3 min) and the artifact citation; `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`
  pins the literal windows and the real-arena budget assertions.

## Desired change

1. Play the shipped one-level deployment in the harness: the hex's
   aggression-selected level through the arena's per-level mode, measuring the
   `level_cleared` tick as the deployment's length.
2. Redefine the outcome model for one level: cleared level = captured,
   early death = loss, and a retry costs the replayed deployment's measured
   length (the 2-minute between-sortie allowance unchanged).
3. Regenerate `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` from the shipped code.
4. Reconcile GDD §8.2 and the docs guards with the regenerated numbers, and
   open a linked rebalancing item for every ring whose budget no longer holds.

  duration from `level_cleared`, captured/loss semantics, retry minutes from
  the measurement) and its module documentation.

  shared seam (read the emitted event; do not fork a second level-completion
  rule).

  semantics, determinism and the regenerated budget verdicts.
- `scripts/ring-timing.mjs`, `scripts/ring-timing.test.ts` — CLI report/docs

- `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` — regenerated artifact (never

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 — measured table, playstyle numbers and

- `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` — the docs guard's means, windows and

- **Expected (not a surprise): both rings may now miss their budgets.** The

- **Risk: off-by-one level completion.** The `level_cleared` tick is emitted on

- **Risk: fidelity gap understates a real sortie.** The arena simulates no

- **Assumption: the aggression → level mapping, ring data, loadout model,

- **Assumption: the competent bot is the measurement line** (unchanged from the

# Capture/scripted setup grants loadout to the player only, so HUD upgrade rows omit it

> **Discovered while addressing AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9** (discovered-from:AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9) — the capture/scripted-setup counterpart of the hangar-war deployment fix.

## Problem statement

`applySceneSetup` (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) grants capture/scripted setup
weapons only through `Player.equipWeapon(id, true)`, bypassing the
`EffectsRegistry`. Gyms that render the shared HUD build their upgrade rows from
`EffectsRegistry.activeWeapons()`, so a capture's permanent weapon has no row in
the upgrade list. The slot budget (`Loadout n/6`) counts it, but the visible list
does not — the same mismatch that AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 fixed on the hangar-war
deployment path.

## Users

**Player running a gym with a capture setup that grants permanent weapons.**

> As a player running a gym whose capture setup grants permanent weapons, when I
> see the HUD upgrade list I expect it to show every permanent weapon I start
> with, so the list matches the `Loadout n/6` count and I can see what I have.

**Maintainer / future agent.**

> As a maintainer, I want capture/scripted setup permanent grants to run through
> the same grant seam as every other permanent grant, so the HUD, the player
> levels and the effect state can never drift apart again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gym (or scene) that applies a capture setup containing permanent weapons via
  `applySceneSetup` reports one slot-counted HUD upgrade row per granted weapon,
  matching a live-play run granted the same weapons through
  `grantPermanentWeapon`.
- The setup applier's documented ability to pre-grant more than
  `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` kinds is preserved (the capture divergence is unchanged).
- A regression test covers a setup-granted permanent weapon reaching both the
  `Player` and the `EffectsRegistry`.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Gyms that apply a capture setup with permanent weapons show those weapons in the
HUD upgrade list, so the list and the `Loadout n/6` count agree at a glance —
the same parity the hangar-war fix achieved for deployed loadouts.

## Constraints

- **The fix belongs in the shared applier `applySceneSetup`.** Gyms are the
  consumers; the applier lives in `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`. No gym is
  changed directly — only the applier's seam interface.
- **One permanent-grant seam.** Grants go through `grantPermanentWeapon`
  (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts`) — the shared seam already used by hold-full
  rewards and checkpoint-resume replay.
- **The six-slot cap divergence stays.** A setup may pre-grant more than
  `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` kinds; the applier never consults the slot pool (AH-0MVVJS34M00551ES).
- **No second HUD data path.** The fix must not make the HUD derive weapon rows
  from the slot model; the HUD keeps rendering registry state.
- **Gyms with no player remain unchanged.** `applySceneSetup` already returns
  early for `getPlayer() === null`; no additional guard needed.
- **`hangarDeployment.ts` stays Phaser-free.** The registry reaches the applier
  through a structural seam, matching the pattern established by that module.

## Existing state

- `applySceneSetup` (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) loops
  `setup.player.weapons` calling `player.equipWeapon(id, true)` — no registry
  grant. Same pattern for `weaponLevels`.
- Gyms call it via `{ getPlayer: () => this.player }` or `{ getPlayer: () => null }`;
  no registry seam is passed today.
- `CombatCoreScene._adoptCaptureSetup` (:336) is the central gym caller — it
  passes `this.player` from a `CombatCoreScene` subclass.
- `PlayScene` (:1419) also calls `applySceneSetup` with `this.player`.
- `grantPermanentWeapon` (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts:80`) has the signature
  `(weaponId, effectsRegistry, player)` — exactly the two-surface grant needed.
- `PermanentWeaponRegistry` (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts:60`) exposes
  `applyWeapon(id, permanent?): boolean` — a minimal structural interface that
  `EffectsRegistry` satisfies.
- **Precedent fix for the identical class of bug on the hangar-war path:**
  AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 extended `HangarWarDeploymentSeams` with an optional
  registry seam and routed through `grantPermanentWeapon`.
- The hangar-war fix (`applyHangarWarDeployment`) still only grants through the
  registry seam it now exposes — it does **not** call `player.equipWeapon` itself,
  delegating entirely to `grantPermanentWeapon`. The scripted setup currently
  grants **only** through `player.equipWeapon`, so both surfaces (registry +
  player) must be touched.

## Desired change

# Tests: one-level deployment semantics (AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A child 1)

**Test-first item.** Pin the *new* deployment semantics in tests **before** any
production change lands, so the harness change in the sibling item is driven by
a failing specification rather than by convention.

Parent: Re-measure ring timing for one-level hex deployments
(AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A). Blocked by **In HexMap killing the mini-boss wins the
hex (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2)**: the behaviour under measurement does not exist on
`dev` yet, so this item is parked rather than closed.

## Context

`createArenaDeploymentRunner` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) currently plays the
**classic campaign slice** (`campaign: true`, `campaignLevels:
campaignFromLevel(campaign, request.level)`) and derives a deployment's length
from `result.ticksSimulated × dt`, with `captured = result.won ||
result.ticksSimulated >= request.ticks` — i.e. "survived the 300 s window".
That model no longer describes the game: a deployment is one hex, one level,
played as a **five-wave sortie** (the level's first four regular waves plus its
mini-boss on wave 5).

The arena **already** supports the seam this needs: per-level mode
(`runArena({ level })`, `buildLevelWavePlan`) emits `level_cleared` on the tick
the final wave is detected clear (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, per-level wave gate),
and the event record carries `tick`. Per-level mode keeps ticking after the
level clears and its `won` is `lives > 0 && aliveHostiles === 0` (a lingering
asteroid keeps it false), so **neither `ticksSimulated` nor `won` may be used**
for the deployment's duration or outcome.

## Scope (tests only — no production edit)

Add a `describe('ring timing: the one-level deployment model')` block to
`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` that fails until the sibling implementation
item lands, pinning:

- **Duration** — a deployment's length is the tick of its level's
  `level_cleared` event × `dt`; the one-tick emission convention is pinned
  literally so a later refactor cannot silently shift every deployment.
- **Outcome** — a run that reaches `level_cleared` is **captured**; a
  `player_death` before it is a **loss**, charged its own measured length.
- **Not-from-the-run-fields** — a case where the level clears but the run keeps
  ticking to `config.ticks` (and `won` is false because an asteroid lingers)
  still measures the clear tick, not the run length.
- **Retry price** — a lost deployment's retry charge is the replayed
  deployment's own measured length × `retriesPerLoss`; the flat
  `DEFAULT_RETRY_MINUTES` (300 s) is no longer the retry price.
- **Between-sortie allowance** — still a flat, documented **2 minutes**,
  pinned literally.
- **Re-capture price (Q1 = a)** — the rush line's exposure allowance charges a
  re-capture the line's measured mean deployment **+ the 2-minute visit**,
  not the retired 18 000-tick window.
- **Determinism** — the same seeds and options produce an identical report
  (deployment seconds, retry minutes, re-capture minutes and totals).

Use an injected fake runner (`RingTimingOptions.runDeployment`) for the model
semantics and one small real-arena case for the `level_cleared` seam. Keep the
new block under 30 s of wall time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` contains a one-level-deployment test block whose cases cover duration, captured/loss, the not-from-`ticksSimulated`/`won` guard, retry price, the 2-minute between-sortie allowance, the re-capture price and determinism.
- Every new case fails on the pre-change harness (red-first evidence recorded in a comment: the assertion messages, not a pasted log) and names the parent work item in the block's doc comment.
- No production file is modified by this item (`git show --stat` shows only the test file).
- The test block runs in under 30 s and introduces no new test-time random source.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- The full project test suite passes once the sibling implementation item has landed (expected to be red on this item alone, which is recorded in the item's completion comment).

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — the new one-level-deployment test block (the only file this item edits).
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` — read-only reference: the current campaign-slice runner and the model inputs the tests pin.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — read-only reference: the per-level wave gate that emits `level_cleared` with its tick.

## Coordination (2026-11-13): the one-level deployment is a five-wave sortie

The deployment this test block pins is the shipped **five-wave sortie**, not a
full ten-wave level: one hex, the aggression-selected level truncated by
`truncateCampaignForDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`,
`DEPLOYMENT_WAVE_COUNT = 5`, AH-0MWDCBVQ700579WS on `dev`) — first four
regular waves plus the wave-5 mini-boss composition. The arena per-level mode
plays the level's authored waves and emits `level_cleared` when the **fifth**
wave's composition clears (the mini-boss entity is not simulated — the
fidelity gap stated in the parent item). Pin that truncated wave plan (learn
the count from the same helper, never a hard-coded 5/10) rather than the
wave-10 model the prose above describes.

## Impact

A Hangar War player's ring time is now measured from the five-wave sorties they actually fly — these red-first tests pin that one-level deployment model before the harness change lands, so the re-measured ring budgets describe real play instead of the retired campaign-slice model.

# Implement: harness plays the one-level deployment (AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A child 2)

Parent: Re-measure ring timing for one-level hex deployments
(AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A). Prerequisite: **Tests: one-level deployment semantics**.

## Context

The committed baseline (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`) models a
deployment as the campaign **slice** from the hex's aggression-selected level to
the campaign's final boss. The mini-boss ending (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2) turns a
deployment into exactly one campaign level — a **five-wave sortie** (the
level's first four regular waves plus its mini-boss on wave 5,
`truncateCampaignForDeployment`), so every measured number and every derived ring window moves. This
item changes the model; it does **not** change the aggression mapping
(`hexDifficultyProfile`), the authored ring data, the loadout resolution, the
retake chance or the 2-minute between-sortie allowance.

## Desired change

1. `createArenaDeploymentRunner` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) plays the
   **shipped one-level deployment**: `runArena` in per-level mode at
   `request.level` (the hex's aggression-selected level), keeping the launch
   `startingLoadout`, the seeded balance config and the existing tick cap as the
   run's safety bound.
2. The deployment's **duration** comes from the arena's `level_cleared` event
   tick (`× dt`) — never from `ticksSimulated` and never from `won`, both of
   which describe the tick loop rather than the level.
3. The **outcome** is `captured` when `level_cleared` was observed and `loss`
   when the player died before it.
4. The **retry allowance** charges the replayed deployment's own measured
   length (`measuredMinutes × retriesPerLoss`) instead of the flat
   `DEFAULT_RETRY_MINUTES` (300 s). `DEFAULT_RETRY_MINUTES` must no longer be
   the retry price; either delete it or redefine it as an explicitly documented
   fallback/sensitivity knob with no default use.
5. The **re-capture allowance** (rush line) charges a re-capture the line's
   measured mean deployment + the 2-minute visit, replacing the retired
   18 000-tick window (producer ruling Q1 = a on the parent item).
6. The module documentation and code comments state the new model end to end
   (`## What is measured, what is modelled` and `## Fidelity boundary`): one
   level played as the shipped **five-wave sortie** (the first four regular waves
   plus the wave-5 mini-boss composition, truncated by
   `truncateCampaignForDeployment` — never a hard-coded 5/10), ending on the
   wave-5 composition clear; the mini-boss encounter's own
   duration is **not** modelled; retries cost the measured replay; re-captures
   cost the measured mean + visit.

**Do not** fork a second level-completion rule or change arena semantics: read
the emitted event. If simulating past the clear makes the regeneration
impractically slow, record the measured wall-clock cost and file a follow-up
item rather than changing `runArena` in this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `createArenaDeploymentRunner` runs the arena in per-level mode at `request.level` and derives each deployment's `seconds` from the `level_cleared` event tick; no path reads `ticksSimulated` or `won` for a deployment's duration or outcome.
- A `level_cleared` deployment is reported `captured`; a death before it is reported as a loss with the death's measured length; a lingering asteroid/hazard after the clear changes neither.
- A lost deployment's retry charge equals its own measured length × `retriesPerLoss`, and `DEFAULT_RETRY_MINUTES` is no longer charged by default (its doc comment or removal says so).
- The rush line's re-capture allowance charges the line's measured mean deployment + the documented 2-minute between-sortie visit; the 2-minute allowance itself is unchanged.
- The retry allowance charges the replayed deployment's own measured length instead of the fixed 5-minute window, the between-sortie allowance stays at the documented 2 minutes, a rush-line re-capture is charged the line's measured mean deployment plus the same 2-minute visit, and both allowances are stated in the harness documentation and pinned by a test.
- The module documentation states the one-level deployment, the measured `level_cleared` duration, the measured replay cost, the measured-mean re-capture cost and the unmodelled mini-boss encounter.
- No arena semantic change: `git show --stat` touches no other module's behaviour, or, if a shared seam proves unavoidable, the change is minimal, documented and covered by an arena test.
- The new model's tests pass and the full project test suite passes with the change.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` — the deployment runner (per-level mode, `level_cleared` duration/outcome), the retry and re-capture allowances, and the module documentation.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — read-only: the `level_cleared` event the runner reads (no second level-completion rule).
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — the pinned semantics this item must turn green.

## Coordination (2026-11-13): the harness plays the shipped five-wave sortie

The deployment `createArenaDeploymentRunner` plays is the shipped **five-wave
sortie** (AH-0MWDCBVQ700579WS, on `dev`): the aggression-selected level's
first four regular waves plus the wave-5 mini-boss composition, truncated with
the same pure helper the game uses (`truncateCampaignForDeployment`,
`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`, `DEPLOYMENT_WAVE_COUNT = 5`) —
never a hard-coded 5 or 10. The harness keeps the arena's per-level mode (it
plays the level's authored waves) but must ensure the deployment's wave set is
the truncated one; if that needs a minimal shared arena seam (e.g. the wave
plan / level definition the per-level mode builds), it is allowed under the
"No arena semantic change" acceptance criterion when it is minimal, documented
and covered by an arena test. `level_cleared` then fires on the tick the
fifth wave's composition clears; the mini-boss encounter itself is not
simulated (the unmodelled fidelity gap).

## Impact

The ring-timing evidence now measures the sortie a player actually flies — one hex, one level, ending on the wave-5 mini-boss composition clear — so the Hangar War pacing budgets can be re-ruled from real measured numbers instead of a campaign slice that no longer ships.

levels past the hex's own), so a ring missing its window is the **expected**
outcome, not a defect in the new model — and the parent item's AC3 forbids
silently re-wording a missed budget: each missed ring becomes its own linked

shipped game measures, and a window change is a separate design decision.

   `missed` per ring with the measured figure and the delta to the window.

   item carrying: the measured figure (mean + min–max), the window, the delta,

   attributable to the one-level model, and the options available (re-author the

# Goal

As a player, I want hulls to be able to grant **extra upgrade bays** (more equipment/loadout slots than the base hull) as a special-reward axis, so the special-mission reward space is not limited to more hit points.

Follow-on from the producer's answer to Q2 on **AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55** ("2. A — create a work item to add upgrade bays"): the special-missions item ships its first reward as a hull with extra hit points; the **upgrade-bay concept does not yet exist in the data model** (HullRunStats carries only startingLives + speedMultiplier; upgrades are armour/firepower/systems), so extending the run-stats/loadout model for upgrade bays is tracked separately here.

Part of the Hangar War's **post-MVP mitigation backlog** (discovered-from:AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55, recorded in `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and GDD §8.2).

## Scope

- Introduce an **upgrade-bay concept** to the hangar hull model: a hull authoring how many bays (equipment/loadout slots) it deploys with, resolved into the run loadout and persisted under the existing `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload.
- Futures a hull reward that grants **extra upgrade bays** rather than (or in addition to) extra hit points — the second special reward the design of record names.
- Must reuse the shipped deployment path (`PlayScene` + `src/scenes/core/`) and the pure hangar economy; no second run implementation (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity). Gym coverage `GymHangar`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hull definition can author an upgrade-bay count, and the resolved deployment/loadout honours it (shipped run, no divergent copy).
- The bay count is persisted under the `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload with field-presence migration (no new storage key).
- `GymHangar` exercises the bay/bay-resolution behaviour with the same code as the game.
- Tests pin the bay model, the loadout resolution and the persistence round-trip; full suite green.

## Context gathered (intake, 2026-11-14)

**Duplicate check:** `wl search` for "bay", "upgrade bay", "loadout", "slot" found no item whose ACs overlap this one — the closest items (AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF six-slot cap, AH-0MVVJRRN10038VFR HUD six-slot budget, AH-0MVZ0GGW1004502H upgrade-count off-by-one, and the hangar-loadout items AH-0MWB8VDU4007G1LQ / AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D / AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX) implement the shipped slot/loadout rules this item builds on; none is a duplicate. No overlapping completed item found.

**Potentially related docs:** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (post-MVP list, §"Post-MVP mitigation backlog" names "extra hit points or extra upgrade bays" → AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55); `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 (same backlog wording); `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` (GymHangar parity rows).

**Potentially related work items:** AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55 (parent epic — special missions; Q2 = a shut upgrade bays out of scope into this item); AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE (shipped Build Candidate D parent); AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D (deployments start with no extra weapons — empty loadout legal); AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX (loadout trimmed to the six-slot cap); AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF (six-slot cap model); AH-0MVVJRRN10038VFR (HUD six-slot budget).

**Model research (repo):** `HullRunStats` (`src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`) carries only `startingLives` + `speedMultiplier`; the run's only equipment-slot concept is the shared six-slot pool (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`, `src/core/constants.ts`, consumed by `src/powerups/slots.ts` — drop draw, collection gate, hold-full choice, HUD rows, `capDropIdsToSlotPool`). The hangar loadout (`HangarLoadout` = `{ startingWeapons, modifiers }`, `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) is currently uncapped; the deployment (`buildHangarDeployment` → `HangarWarDeployment`) carries the resolved hull stats forward to `PlayScene`; `applyHangarWarDeployment` trims starting weapons to the six-slot cap. No "upgrade bay" semantics exist anywhere — the term appears only in the design-of-record backlog wording.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 (upgrade-bay semantics) — OPEN QUESTION (needs producer)

**Q1 asked:** The design of record names "extra upgrade bays" as a hull reward axis but never defines what a bay *is*. The run's only equipment-slot concept today is the shipped six-slot power-up/weapon pool (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`), and the hangar loadout (`startingWeapons`/`modifiers`) is uncapped. What does one extra upgrade bay grant in the run?
Options: (a) **one extra shared run loadout slot** — a bay hull deploys with a raised equipment cap (6 + N, e.g. 7–8) for that deployment; the shared slot accounting (`powerups/slots.ts`: drop draw, collection gate, choice, HUD, pre-grant trim) is parameterised by the deployment's bay count; (b) **one extra starting-weapon slot in the hangar loadout selector** — the bay count expands how many distinct starting weapons a deployment may be equipped with (the run still trims to the shared cap during play); (c) **one extra hangar modifier slot** — expands the active loadout's modifier capacity; (d) other.

**Recommended:** (a) — the run's shared slots are the game's actual equipment slots, so like extra hit points the reward is felt *inside* the run; (b)/(c) only widen the pre-deployment pick list and are bounded by the shipped cap in-run. Base bay count = 6 (the shipped `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`); a save/payload without the field reads as 6 (field-presence).

### Q2 (ship a bay hull now?) — OPEN QUESTION (needs producer)

**Q2 asked:** How far does this item go? Options: (a) **model + mechanics + one shipped catalogue bay hull** (e.g. `hull-4`, authoring a bay count, grantable via `resolveHexGrant` like `hull-3`) so the axis is exercised end-to-end by `GymHangar`; wiring the ring's special-mission rotation to *offer* it stays a follow-on; (b) **also wire the bay hull as the second special reward** in the shipped rotation/offer surface within this item; (c) **model + mechanics only** — the bay hull exists only as test/fixture data, the real reward hull decided at planning.

**Recommended:** (a) — AC1/AC3 demand the resolved deployment honour an authored bay count through the shipped run with no divergent copy, which needs at least one real authored bay hull to exercise; the rotation/offer surface belongs to the special-missions epic (AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55, already in review) and is a natural follow-on.

### Q3 (where the bay count is persisted) — OPEN QUESTION (needs producer)

**Q3 asked:** AC2 says the bay count is "persisted under the `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload with field-presence migration (no new storage key)". Options: (a) **authored in the catalogue only** (`HullRunStats.upgradeBays`), and the resolved count is carried forward as launch data in the deployment payload (`HangarWarDeployment.upgradeBays`, absent = 6) — the persisted hangar already records the active hull id, so no storage change; (b) **also stored on the payload** (`HangarState`/`HangarWarPayload` gains an explicit bay field, field-presence migrated) so the run honours a stored count independent of the catalogue.

**Recommended:** (a) — the active hull id is already the single source of truth; storing the count too creates a second source that can drift from the catalogue. Field-presence then applies to the launch/deployment payload parse exactly as `startingLives`/`speedMultiplier` do today.

## Problem

When `implement.py drive` spawns a child session that dies before writing anything (e.g. a transient provider error — `Provider finish_reason: error`), the child is left `in-progress` with an empty worktree (0 dirty files, 0 commits ahead of dev). The next `drive`/`parent` run then calls `_child_main_checkout_violation()` for that child, which finds `_git_path_has_changes(wt)` false (correctly — no work) and therefore attributes **pre-existing dirt in the main checkout and in other items' sibling worktrees** to the failed child. The run fails closed with a long 'produced changes in the sibling worktree …' message naming paths the child never touched.

## Impact during AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP

Recovering child AH-0MWEXI5460080WEI required a manual `implement.py abort` before the drive would proceed; the guard's message blamed `src/test/playSceneBootGuard.test.ts` (main checkout) and files in `wl-AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G`, `wl-AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q`, `wl-AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA` and `/tmp/hw-base-check` — all other sessions' work.

## Acceptance criteria

- A driven child left `in-progress` by a **spawn failure** (no changes in its worktree, no commits ahead) is treated as startable-again/reset, not as a placement violation, so the next `drive` re-spawns it without manual `abort`.
- The placement guard distinguishes 'this child wrote elsewhere' from 'this child wrote nothing and other surfaces happen to be dirty' — the latter must not fail the chain.
- Regression test: a spawn-failed child plus a dirty main checkout and a dirty sibling worktree does not produce a `_child_main_checkout_violation`; a child that genuinely wrote only into a sibling worktree still does.
- No weakening of the genuine cross-worktree-write detection (SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I).
